lifecycle: Ansina is a producer only. It does not read this bucket back and names no consumer. Contract changes arrive as new GitHub issues filed against the ansina repo, never the reverse.

stability_promise.minor_change: a new family, or a new optional/nullable field on an existing family — does not bump schema_version
stability_promise.breaking_change: a field removed, renamed, or changed in type/semantics, or a bucket key layout change — bumps schema_version; the prior corpus-schema-v<N>.json is never deleted or overwritten

changelog.2: issue #67 — added a host=<id>/ key-prefix segment ahead of dt=<date>/ for kind=telemetry/ and kind=runlog/, resolving v1's documented no-host-attribution gap. No field in any per-family schema changed.
changelog.3: issue #68 — added idle_total/act_total/escalate_total to telemetry_sample: three lifetime, monotonically non-decreasing per-decision counters, letting a reader reconstruct the exact idle/act/escalate counts for any window instead of inferring them from last_decision alone, which a 60s default sample_interval_seconds against a 30s tick cadence observes at only a 2:1 (undercounted) ratio. No field removed or renamed; bumped for discoverability of the fix rather than treated as a silent minor addition.
changelog.4: issue #76 — added a new family, opencode_event (host=<id>/kind=opencode/), the third telemetry shape: one JSON line per OpenCode run-lifecycle event, produced by ansina.opencode.telemetry.OpencodeTelemetryWriter. A new family is a non-breaking minor addition per the stability promise's own text and would not on its own require a bump; bumped anyway for discoverability, the same reasoning issue #68 already established for its own additive change. No existing family's fields changed. This family was wired into nothing as of this issue.
changelog.5: issue #79 — populated opencode_event's own already-reserved intervention event with real fields (action/outcome/detail), the Heart's bounded, deterministic interventions on the OpenCode executor (ansina.heart.tick.opencode_intervention_handler.OpencodeInterventionHandler, gated by [heart.tick] opencode_interventions, default false). Populating an already-reserved, already-documented event name is a non-breaking addition per the stability promise's own text; bumped anyway, the identical discoverability reasoning issues #68/#76 already established. No existing field changed or removed.

bucket_key_layout.host_attribution: <id> is ansina.dev.vector.resolve_host_id's result — the operator-configured [telemetry] host_id when set, else this host's own socket.gethostname(), both sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9._-]. bench/soak are unaffected by this issue — each bench/soak report already carries its own host/commit/branch provenance fields (see bench_report/triage_bench_report below). opencode ships host-attributed from birth (issue #76), unlike telemetry/runlog's own v1-to-v2 history.

fields.suite: string ("tick") — issue #13: present from this issue onward; absent on earlier reports means "tick", the only suite that existed then. Discriminates from the sibling triage_bench_report family below, which shares this same kind_prefix.

triage_bench_report.note: issue #13, a gated experiment whose port (ansina.heart.triage) is wired into no route or the tick loop — this family's own data proves or refutes adoption, nothing more. Shares kind=bench/ with bench_report above; distinguished by the suite field ("triage") and its own field set.

fields.metrics.brain_calls_saved_fraction: float [0,1] (vs. the always-escalate baseline, which saves 0; reported, never gated)
fields.metrics.confusion: object<string,object<string,int>> (expected class -> actual class or "unparsed" -> count)

samples.jsonl.note: no circuit-breaker counters and no per-decision totals — GET /heart/tick doesn't expose them; contrast with telemetry_sample below

run.log.shape: same as log_line family below, one JSON object per line

journal.json.shape: verbatim GET /heart/journal?limit=500 response body — same shape as JournalPage, see note in contract doc

soak-<date>.json.shape: small run-metadata summary, not the full report

fields.rss_kib: int | null (peak ru_maxrss, NOT instantaneous — see divergence note)
fields.idle_total: int | null (lifetime, monotonically non-decreasing since tick loop start — issue #68)
fields.act_total: int | null (same shape as idle_total — issue #68)
fields.escalate_total: int | null (same shape as idle_total — issue #68)

divergence_from_soak_samples_jsonl: rss_kib is peak (monotonically non-decreasing), not instantaneous — not bit-comparable sample-for-sample against soak's samples.jsonl
every field nullable (sampling runs independently of [heart]/[heart.tick]); soak's samples.jsonl has no such case
telemetry_sample.exact_decision_counts: issue #68: idle_total/act_total/escalate_total are running totals, not deltas since the prior sample — a reader computes the exact count for any window by subtracting the relevant field's value at the window's start from its value at the window's end, unaffected by a missed or delayed sample. Needed because last_decision alone, sampled at the default 60s sample_interval_seconds against a 30s tick cadence, observes only ~1 in 2 ticks (confirmed at exactly 2.00 ticks per sample against one real day's telemetry).
telemetry_sample.note: no field on this record carries the host — attribution is purely via the host=<id>/ key-prefix segment above (issue #67)

log_line.shape: one JSON object per line, identical to the daemon's own primary log stream and to soak's run.log

fields.request_id: string (present only inside an HTTP request's correlation scope)
fields.extra: object (present only when the log call passed extra=...; string leaves redacted recursively)
fields.exception: string (present only on an exception log, redacted)
fields.stack: string (present only when stack info was captured, redacted)

log_line.note: no field on this record carries the host either — same host=<id>/ key-prefix attribution as telemetry_sample above (issue #67)

opencode_event.note: issue #76 — the third telemetry shape (event-driven, one line per run-lifecycle event) alongside telemetry_sample (interval) and log_line (log mirror) above, through the same generic SpooledRotatingWriter under its own "opencode" file-prefix family. Issue #79 populates the intervention event — see event_specific_fields.intervention below.

fields.run_id: string | null (stable across every line for one run; null only for an intervention line whose action — pause_intake — has no single triggering run)
fields.seq: int (0-based, monotonic per run_id; 0 with no running counter when run_id is null — see gap_detection below)

submitted.prompt: string (truncated preview, never the full unbounded prompt)

run_event.payload: string (the full redacted+truncated captured line — the lossless fallback)
run_event.tool: string (optional — present only when the payload carried it, a tool call)

opencode_event.intervention_producer: issue #79: ansina.heart.tick.opencode_intervention_handler.OpencodeInterventionHandler, gated by [heart.tick] opencode_interventions (default false). This is the supervision record — the opencode run's own execution events (run_event/the terminal statuses above) are unaffected by an intervention attempted against them; a retry/nudge is a new run with its own full event stream, linked back to the original only via opencode_runs.retry_of (not a field on this telemetry record).
opencode_event.truncation_and_redaction: a line exceeding the writer's own max_line_bytes cap (re-asserted independently of whatever truncation already happened at the adapter boundary) falls back to a minimal envelope (t/run_id/session_id/seq/event plus truncated: true) rather than a bare mid-JSON cut. Every line is also passed through ansina.logging.redaction.redact in full, uniformly — the first code path that ever redacts RunRequest.prompt at all.
opencode_event.gap_detection: for one run_id, seq must be a contiguous 0-based sequence (0, 1, 2, ...) with no value skipped — a reader detects a dropped line (an upload-side truncation, a crash mid-run) by finding a break in consecutive seq values within that run_id's own lines. seq is scoped per run_id, not global — two concurrent runs each start their own counter at 0.

harness_authority: ansina.heart.eval remains the authoritative in-repo tick-decision harness; it renders every fixture through the real heart.tick.snapshot.build_prompt and heart.tick.decision.try_parse_decision. No external tool recommended below replaces it — each operates only on finished results this harness already produced.
analysis_layer_tooling: evaluated during issue #63's planning; the recommendation and reasoning are maintained privately and intentionally not published in this document — see docs/ml/corpus-contract.md's own 'Analysis-layer tooling' section for why

ml_readiness.does_not_support: learning a better tick-decision policy — no non-idle ground truth exists in the live corpus beyond fault-injection fixtures
paths_forward: fault-injection fixtures producing labelled non-idle samples at scale (issue #72)
the Brain's own response to an escalated tick as a supervisory label (issue #64)
the Heart's own bounded intervention outcomes (issue #79) as a second, OpenCode-specific supervisory signal
